newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dollar down, bonds rise on data barrage.
newsitem.headline: Australian dollar down, bonds rise on data barrage.

text.p: The Australian dollar fell and bonds firmed after the Australian Bureau of Statistics issued three sets of data for first quarter balance of payments as well as April retail trade and motor vehicle registrations.

The dollar was quoted at US$0.7662/67 compared with US$0.7677/82 just before the data releases, while June 10-year bond futures were at 92.485 against a pre-data 92.445. September bills also rose, moving to 94.57 from 94.53.
Retail trade fell 1.7 percent against an expected 0.5 percent rise and 0.3 percent fall in March.
April motor registrations fell 6.0 percent compared with a 1.3 percent rise in March and an expected flat outcome.
Balance of payments showed a A$4.587 billion deficit after the A$5.3 billion shortfall in the December quarter and compared with median forecasts for a A$4.8 billion deficit.
